members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs modify the memory-stream buffer size used for stdio_server's write_stream in src/mcp/server/stdio.py. The underlying issue is that a zero-capacity write_stream can cause a handler to block when trying to queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g., a progress notification). #2215 generalizes this by adding read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters (both still defaulting to 0, i.e. no behavior change unless a caller explicitly opts in). #2654 fixes the same code path directly by hardcoding the write stream's buffer to 1, with an accompanying BlockingStdout test that reproduces the deadlock/blocking scenario during progress notifications and verifies the fix.

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify validate_tool_use_result_messages() in src/mcp/server/validation.py to handle the case where a previous assistant message contains tool_use but the current message has no tool_result at all — but they implement opposite, mutually exclusive behaviors on the same lines. #2962 adds `has_tool_results` to the outer guard so the id-matching check (and any error) is skipped entirely when there are no tool_results, explicitly citing SEP-1577 and issue #2960: a tool_use is NOT required to be followed by a tool_result, so nothing should be raised. #3053 keeps the original guard and instead adds a new explicit raise ('tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks') when has_tool_results is false — i.e. it keeps raising, just with a clearer message. These cannot both be merged since they produce contradictory outcomes (raise vs. no raise) for the identical input case. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 first splits the header into distinct auth-scheme segments (_split_www_authenticate_segments) and only then extracts params for the matching scheme (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic ..., Bearer ...').
